extracted.intended_audience: children's librarians, picture-book illustrators, publishers, and award submitters
extracted.subtask_description: Official terms, definitions, eligibility rules, submission procedures, and evaluative criteria used by the ALSC Caldecott Committee to select the Randolph Caldecott Medal and Honor Books for distinguished American picture books for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal award scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal shall be awarded annually to the artist of the most distinguished American picture book for children published in the United States during the preceding year. Honor Books may be named; these shall be books that are also truly distinguished. There are no limitations as to the character of the picture book except that the illustrations be original work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the object of the award (artist of a single, distinguished American picture book published in the U.S. in the prior year). Honors (runners-up) may be named as 'Honor Books.' Illustrations must be original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist eligibility (citizen or resident)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Award is restricted to artists who are citizens or residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency (see definition) or citizenship required; casual or occasional visitors are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee consideration limited to eligible books
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee in its deliberations is to consider only the books eligible for the award, as specified in the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee should not consider ineligible works or extraneous factors outside the stated eligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: picture book provides visual experience
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'picture book for children' as distinguished from other books with illustrations, is one that essentially provides the child with a visual experience. A picture book has a collective unity of story line, theme, or concept, developed through the series of pictures of which the book is comprised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the primacy of pictures and a unified visual development of story/theme/concept rather than merely decorative illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: children as potential audience and age range
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'picture book for children' is one for which children are a potential audience. The book displays respect for children's understandings, abilities, and appreciations. Children are defined as persons of ages up to and including fourteen and picture books for this entire age range are to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility and evaluation should take into account whether the book is appropriate and respectful toward children up to age 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'distinguished'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Distinguished' is defined as marked by eminence and distinction: noted for significant achievement; marked by excellence in quality; marked by conspicuous excellence or eminence; individually distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The central quality the committee seeks; language stresses notable, conspicuous, and high-quality achievement rather than mere popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist defined (illustrator or co-illustrators) and posthumous award
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist is the illustrator or co-illustrators. The artist may be awarded the medal posthumously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who receives the medal; allows posthumous recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original Work requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Original Work' means that illustrations reprinted or compiled from other sources are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations must be original to the book (not previously published elsewhere or compiled).

rubrics_metrics.name: American picture book publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 'American picture book in the United States' specifies that books originally published in other countries are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original publication must be in the United States; translations or works first published abroad are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication year eligibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Published . . . in the preceding year' means that the book has a publication date in that year, was available for purchase in that year, and has a copyright date no later than that year. If a book is published prior to its year of copyright as stated in the book, it shall be considered in its year of copyright as stated in the book. The intent is that every book be eligible for consideration, but that no book be considered in more than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes precise rules to determine the single year of eligibility based on publication/copyright and availability for purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident definition
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Resident' specifies that author has established and maintained residence in the United States as distinct from being a casual or occasional visitor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency implies established, ongoing residence, not temporary visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision limited to specified calendar year's books (not artist's body of work)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'only the books eligible for the Award' specifies that the committee is not to consider the entire body of the work by an artist or whether the artist has previously won the award. The committee's decision is to be made following deliberation about books of the specified calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should focus solely on the candidate book for that year, not on the illustrator's career or past honors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of execution and pictorial interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members need to consider: excellence of execution in the artistic technique employed; excellence of pictorial interpretation of story, theme, or concept; appropriateness of style of illustration to the story, theme or concept; delineation of plot, theme, characters, setting, mood or information through the pictures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad set of artistic quality measures covering technique, interpretive clarity, stylistic fit, and how effectively pictures convey narrative/characters/setting/mood or information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of presentation for a child audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members must consider excellence of presentation in recognition of a child audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pictures should be presented in ways that recognize children's perspectives, comprehension, and engagement; presentation quality for children is a required consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic form limitation and self-contained requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The only limitation to graphic form is that the form must be one which may be used in a picture book. The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media (i.e., sound or film equipment) for its enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits diverse graphic techniques provided they work in the picture book medium; disqualifies works requiring external media to be understood/enjoyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary basis: illustrations with consideration of other components
rubrics_metrics.description: Each book is to be considered as a picture book. The committee is to make its decision primarily on the illustration, but other components of a book are to be considered especially when they make a book less effective as a children's picture book. Such other components might include the written text, the overall design of the book, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration quality is central, but poor text/design that undermines the pictorial presentation may be taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award intent: not for didactic intent or popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: The committee should keep in mind that the award is for distinguished illustrations in a picture book and for excellence of pictorial presentation for children. The award is not for didactic intent or for popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that instructional aims or mass-market popularity are not valid substitutes for artistic distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit a book for consideration for the Caldecott Award, one must review the terms and criteria for the award and send one copy of the work to the ALSC office. Another copy must be submitted to the award committee chair. Additional copies may be sent to each of the fifteen committee members, but it is not required. The deadline for submission is December 31 of the publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirements for entering a book for consideration: required copies, optional additional copies, and the submission cutoff date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee composition, duties, and voting process
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year a committee of 15 members, all children's librarians chosen for their critical ability, leadership, and service to children, reads and evaluates submissions, writes reviews and annotations, meets at mid-winter for extensive discussion and votes, and selects a winner by majority support; after selecting a winner, discussion continues to decide whether to select Honor Books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the human-process standards for evaluation: membership qualifications, workload expectations, deliberation and majority-vote requirement, and Honor Book selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor Books designation and seals
rubrics_metrics.description: Books cited as worthy of attention may be referred to as Honor Books (formerly 'runners-up'); silver facsimile seals with the designation are printed and may be placed on the honor books similar to gold seals of the medal winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative practice for recognizing and marking deserving non-winning titles; terminology and physical seals.
